data.why: the repository bundles a synthetic 26-record RIS set with a matching protocol and 15 known decisions, which is exactly the example the app's own 'use bundled example' checkbox loads, and copying it also lets the browser agent exercise the file-upload path.

goals: upload a records export (RIS) and a review protocol, then run the mock backend to screen titles and abstracts without needing a model or GPU
calibrate an exclusion threshold against known include/exclude decisions and see how many of the known inclusions are kept, with a Wilson confidence interval
review the ranked list of records split into include, uncertain and exclude, and read the one-line reasons for borderline records
inspect the PRISMA 2020 counts and methods paragraph generated for the run
open the self-contained HTML report and download the screened records, results CSV, and PRISMA summary as a zip

review.summary: The tree states the tool's purpose accurately: cut title-and-abstract screening work while keeping a target recall of known inclusions, then document the cut for PRISMA. It covers almost everything the Streamlit UI offers, and 11 of the 12 screens I checked fully support their nodes. Before filing it needs light restructuring: fix the t2/t3 branch logic, give deduplication its own task, move the protocol-bug detour into notes, split the oversized f7 feature, and record the recall-percentage inconsistency the checker found.
